limits: Shared installation setting takes effect on next sign-in. Device remains an installation; the signed-in member is the accountable identity.

ordered_actions: Home > Status: show current personnel status and department stats.
Press and hold a status for 2 seconds; for configured multi-step statuses choose Calls, Stations or POI destination, add required/optional Note, hold to submit.
Use Show all statuses versus Show next statuses only to explain configured workflow.
Home > Staffing: tap to set staffing; long press to Add a note; use full staffing sheet where note is required.
Home > active Call: View Call Details / Clear Active Call; show due-check card and weather banner.

prerequisites: Personnel status/staffing definitions; stations/POIs/calls; user permissions; other demo personnel and units.

ordered_actions: Settings > Active Unit > Select Unit > choose an accessible apparatus; verify Current Unit.
Open sidebar unit/status/roles cards.
Press and hold status for 2 seconds; choose Calls, Stations or POI destination and note as required; Hold to submit.
Show next statuses versus Show all statuses; verify current status changed.
Roles card > Unit Role Assignments > choose personnel per role > Save.
Choose another active unit and show map/status/inventory/roles scope updating.

limits: No active unit means no status controls; no assigned units means admin must add the user to station group. This changes the apparatus status, while Responder changes the individual member status.

ordered_actions: Use New Call floating action button.
Fill Name, Nature, Priority, Type, Note, call location, Contact Name/Info; use fields allowed/required by department policy.
Resolve location by Address, GPS Coordinates, what3words, Plus Code or Select Location on Map; show validation for invalid data.
Choose Destination where configured; choose Scheduled Dispatch Time / Dispatch Time if allowed.
Dispatch To > select personnel, groups, roles, units or Everyone as permitted > Create.
Open menu > Edit Call > change demo details > Save.
Open menu > Close Call > Close Type and optional Close Note; choose Notify everyone on the call deliberately; confirm close.

scenario_variants: Street address versus remote trail coordinate/what3words/plus code
EMS hospital destination versus fire incident location
limits: Visible form fields depend on department policy. Responder additionally exposes external/incident/reference IDs where allowed. Production dispatch can notify real people; recording requires isolated demo data.

ordered_capture_plan.title: Call detail collaboration, check-in and command
ordered_actions: Open Info, Contact, Protocols, Dispatched, Activity tabs.

History: inspect previous calls/location history where supplied.

critical_findings.finding: Responder and Unit have materially different scope; a single shared video is insufficient.

Responder env variables use RESPOND_, Unit uses UNIT_. BASE_API_URL is an origin; API base defaults to origin/api/v4, and persisted custom server overrides it. Both default to QA, so explicitly select local/demo server before capture.
Runtime feature flags are department scoped and fail closed for missing entries. Records requires parent plus app-specific child; ensure seeded demo department enables all desired modules.
Two distinct deployment surfaces: /operations is field workforce/time/cost operations; /records/deployments is external resource order/fill and connector reconciliation. Capture both.
Unit operational time-report approval is disabled by capability; Responder supports approval with server permission.

No standalone training route exists; training can be demonstrated through Responder calendar events, certifications and CE plus published Records. Unit has no shifts, certifications or work-order screen in current source.
Checklist web vault is memory only; browser capture cannot prove secure durable native offline operation after app restart.
Controlled inventory differences need a second witness on web; connector management/reconciliation and F-42 portal submission are web handoffs.

Unit has deliberate web module shims/resolver and mapbox-gl adapter. Responder also has CJS Zustand and several native stubs, but not all native imports are shimmed. Static risks need live launch verification by primary.

potential_web_boot_blockers.status: source-confirmed unshimmed native constructor path; runtime app launch not tested
potential_web_boot_blockers.issue: Responder eagerly imports @notifee/react-native from the livekit store. Its Metro resolver does not shim Notifee. Installed Notifee constructor creates NativeEventEmitter(this.native); the native getter throws Notifee native module not found when browser NativeModules lacks NotifeeApiModule. This is a concrete browser boot hazard until runtime resolution or a patch mitigates it.

callkeep.service.ts eagerly imports Android and iOS implementations and has no .web counterpart; both import react-native-callkeep, unlike Unit dedicated web service/shim. Native event emitter setup can be a browser hazard.
Zustand ESM import.meta.env is a known Metro web issue; both Metro configs force CJS exports. Keep these project configs in effect and clear Metro cache when environment changes.

Valid Mapbox client token/style, API CORS, eventing/SignalR URL/hub routing, HTTPS/secure context for passkeys and browser permission APIs must match selected server. Defaults point to QA and persisted server URL overrides env.

Expo Go does not substitute for a custom native build containing MMKV, Mapbox, CallKeep, BLE and other native plugins. Browser execution can show many forms but cannot validate hardware/PTT, push delivery, background location or OS call UI.

Metro web resolves Notifee/CallKeep/BLE/LiveKit native packages to shims, Countly to dedicated shims and build-time packages to empty module. Web livekit-client can provide browser WebRTC, but native AudioSession methods are no-ops.

Metro stubs LiveKit native components and BLE/Countly; @rnmapbox/maps package contains an actual web Mapbox adapter. Do not claim maps are categorically unavailable on web; validate feature support in live rendering.
